chapter_note: This chapter is largely a systematic cosmological catalogue of twelve judging powers emanated from the Father of Greatness (CORE). The opening dialogue tag is a late hagiographic frame (¶1), and the closing exhortation to the community is pastoral/application (¶16), consistent with the chapter’s strong second-half drift. Two list-items show later institutional/Manichaean-church coloring inside an otherwise cosmic sequence: (a) Jesus the Splendour labelled “father of all the apostles” (¶10), and (b) Light Mind “choos[ing] the holy church” (¶13); these are best treated as MIXED with the ecclesial identifiers removed.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue frame (“Once again… disciples”) characteristic of the Kephalaia’s editorial/hagiographic apparatus.

paragraphs.core_text: Twelve judges exist; the great mighty givers of judgement! They were sent and came from the exalted greatness to this place. They were assigned to different works according to the command that the Judge, who belongs to the greatness, entrusted to all these judges. Now he, the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges, who exists and is established in the aeons of greatness; he is the Father of Greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological exposition: emanation/sending from Greatness; no audience address or institutional identification; establishes the cosmic hierarchy of Judge and judges.

paragraphs.core_text: The first judge is the First Man, he who humiliated the ruler of Darkness in the beginning. He judged him according to a judgement of righteousness; for he had exalted himself against a kingdom that was not his own.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-historical function of a named emanation (First Man) within the Light–Darkness conflict; “righteousness” here serves as a cosmic judicial quality, not pastoral exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The second judge is the Living Spirit, he who came and bore up the Man. He too made a judgement on all the powers of darkness; which had wounded the garments of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal mythic mechanics (rescue/raising; judgement on powers) tied to core Manichaean beings.

paragraphs.core_text: The third judge is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, she who beautified and set up the heavenly part of the universe, according to her pleasure; which [...] her. She judged the rulers above; she fettered and set them firmly in the place that is fitting for them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic architecture and binding of rulers; the entire mapping stays within the cosmological system (heavenly part, rulers above, fitting place).

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth judge is the Great Builder, he who built the new aeon of joy. He judged, according to a judgement of righteousness, the storehouses of the enemy; that death may not well up from this time on. He has constructed a prison for the enemy. Also, upon the crown of the building he has constructed a throne for the First Man and all the fathers of light; they who engaged the struggle with the evil one and were victorious over him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic construction (new aeon, prison, throne) and containment of “death”; still system-internal despite slightly heightened rhetorical tone.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.80⟩
The fifth judge is the great King of Honour, he who dwells and is established in the seventh firmament. He is the judge of all the firmaments who gives a true judgement, according to a judgement of righteousness, upon all the powers and all the kingdoms of the firmaments.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Firmament-level hierarchy and jurisdiction; structured cosmic geography (“seventh firmament… all the firmaments”).

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth judge is [the Th]ird Ambassador, he who came and displayed his image. He purified the light [...] which his own [...] also of the enemy, he has [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Named emanation (Third Ambassador) in a functional cosmic role (image-display; purification of light); lacunae obscure details but register remains cosmological.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh judge is ... ... the worlds [... as he gives the victory to] they who are steadfast; but he condemns the ones who are convicted ... ... he shall become for them the steps of the way (?) [...]; but the convicted he sweeps and casts out to the depths.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological sorting expressed as cosmic judgement (victory/condemnation; casting to depths). No direct audience address or institutional target.

paragraphs.core_text: The eighth judge is Jesus the Splendour, because after the Ambassador had displayed his image and the light was taken [...] a mass of rulers rose up from above and below. Then they sent Jesus the Splendour. He came ... ... he descended and made a judgement in the firmaments. He separated the steadfast from the convicted.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ecclesial/institutional title “the father of all the apostles;” as a later church-identifying gloss that points outside the cosmological system.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is a cosmological mission of Jesus the Splendour within the firmaments; the “apostles” label is a later institutional vocabulary intrusion typical of Mani’s/community framing.

paragraphs.core_text: The ninth judge is the Virgin of Light, [she who took the heart] of the powers by her image, gathering her own ones into her. She makes a judgement on the ruler of the moist, and the ruler of the dry.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Virgin of Light acting through image/attraction; rulers of moist/dry are cosmic divisions (system-internal correspondential structuring).

paragraphs.core_text: The tenth judge is the Judge who dwells in the atmosphere, judging all mankind. He makes a separation between they who are good and they who are evil, setting apart the righteous from the sinners.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Though ethically worded, it still describes a cosmic station (“dwells in the atmosphere”) and its judicial function; no exhortation or institutional identification.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.81⟩
The eleventh judge is the Light Mind, he who shall come and appear in the world. And he separates light from darkness, and sets the truth apart from lawlessness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional application clause “chooses the holy church, and he unveils [...] and” as an ecclesial identification that crosses from cosmos→church.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying item fits the cosmic list (Light Mind; light/dark separation), but the “holy church” insertion is a later editorial application within the list-form.

paragraphs.core_text: The twelfth judge is the great counsel, which is the summons and the obedience, which is appointed in the elements. It is the one that makes a separation between the good and the evil ones. At the end also it can gather itself together and sculpt its own self in the Last Statue. And it separates light from darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly systematic, system-internal eschatological mechanism (elements; end; Last Statue; separation of light/darkness) with impersonal explanatory voice.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the twelve great and mighty judges who were sent. They came from the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges. He is the Father that is hidden and immeasurable, the one who exists; who is established in the aeons of greatness upon the great throne of honour, which is the King of Honour [...] in his kingdom.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic recapitulation/closure returning to the transcendent Father of Greatness; no behavioural address; fits a core summary colophon to the list.

Direct audience address and imperatives (“my beloved ones… you yourselves may walk… Judge…”) with moral exhortation and communal conduct: classic pastoral/application layer, matching the chapter’s second-half drift.
